title: Why Are Blue Eyes Blue?
pause_note: Short format v3 (2026-11-13): 20-30 s, claim first, loop ending

beats: There's no blue pigment in blue eyes.
Every eye colour comes from one brown pigment: melanin.
Blue eyes have almost none in the front layer of the iris.
Tiny fibres there scatter light, and blue scatters the most.
The dark back layer soaks up the rest.
Add a little melanin, and the eye looks green. Add more, brown.
Blue eyes are blue the way the sky is blue.
